headline.title: The next phase of OpenAI’s Education for Countries
headline.summary: OpenAI is expanding its Education for Countries initiative by forming new partnerships and providing teacher training to enhance AI adoption in schools. The program aims to improve global learning outcomes through the development of innovative educational tools.

articles.title: I/O 2026
articles.summary: At Google I/O 2026, the company unveiled new initiatives aimed at enhancing the accessibility and utility of AI technologies for users. The event highlighted a range of announcements focused on improving AI integration across various platforms and services.

articles.title: I/O 2026: Welcome to the agentic Gemini era
articles.summary: Google I/O 2026 introduced the Gemini era, highlighting advancements in AI technology and its applications. The event showcased new features and tools aimed at enhancing user interaction and productivity through AI-driven solutions.

articles.title: Gemini 3.5: frontier intelligence with action
articles.summary: Gemini 3.5 has been introduced as an advanced AI model, enhancing capabilities in text processing and multi-modal tasks. The update focuses on improving intelligence and action-oriented functionalities, positioning it as a significant development in AI technology.

articles.title: Everything new in our Google AI subscriptions, fresh from I/O 2026
articles.summary: Google has announced updates to its AI subscription plans at I/O 2026, introducing enhanced features and benefits while maintaining the same pricing structure. The new offerings aim to provide users with increased capabilities and perks within a single subscription plan.

articles.title: How AI Mode is changing the way people search in the U.S.
articles.summary: The article discusses the impact of AI Mode on search behaviors in the U.S., highlighting how users are increasingly integrating AI tools into their search processes. It features a graphic that visually represents various elements associated with AI-assisted searching.

articles.title: Google just declared itself a contender in AI design at IO 2026
articles.summary: At IO 2026, Google announced its entry into AI design with a new app aimed at making AI tools accessible to a wide range of users, including teachers and small business owners. The initiative reflects Google's commitment to democratizing AI technology for various applications.

articles.title: You can now talk to your Gmail inbox, as seen at Google IO 2026
articles.summary: Google has introduced conversational voice search to its Gmail AI Inbox, allowing users to interact with their emails using voice commands. This feature, showcased at Google IO 2026, enables users to ask Gemini to retrieve specific email information more easily.

articles.title: From teen hacker to Iron Dome researcher, this founder raised $28M to fight AI phishing
articles.summary: Ocean, an email security platform, has raised $28 million to enhance its AI capabilities in detecting phishing and impersonation attempts by analyzing the context of incoming emails. The company aims to leverage advanced technology to combat the growing threat of AI-driven email fraud.

articles.title: Everything Announced at Google I/O 2026: Gemini, Search, Smart Glasses
articles.summary: At Google I/O 2026, the company announced enhancements to its Gemini AI models, improvements to its search functionality, and the integration of AI agents across various platforms. Additionally, new smart glasses are set to be released this fall.

articles.title: GroupAffect-4: A Multimodal Dataset of Four-Person Collaborative Interaction
articles.summary: The article presents GroupAffect-4, a new multimodal dataset designed to analyze affective interactions in four-person collaborative settings. This dataset integrates various signals, including physiology, eye movement, audio, self-reports, and task outcomes, to support comprehensive analysis of individual, interpersonal, and group-level processes in co-located interactions.

articles.title: Using Aristotle API for AI-Assisted Theorem Proving in Lean 4: A Formalisation Case Study of the Grasshopper Problem
articles.summary: This article discusses a case study on the use of the Aristotle API for AI-assisted theorem proving in Lean 4, focusing on the formalization of the Grasshopper problem from the 2009 International Mathematical Olympiad. The study highlights the verification process and the generated Lean artifact, which presents a generalized version of the theorem.
